issues: Dolphin body is filled with coarse dithered/halftone stippling, reading as a noisy point-cloud rather than a smooth lit phosphor creature; this is the single biggest deviation from a real OEL panel.
Bright foggy smudge in the bottom-left corner (around the L/R VU meters) looks like an over-bloomed persistence artifact and pulls the eye away from the dolphin, breaking the intended hierarchy.
Afterglow beneath the dolphin is a messy vertical fog smear instead of a short, directional persistence trail tied to the leap's motion.
Dolphin head/rostrum definition is weak — the snout dissolves into grain, so the front silhouette is less graceful than the tail end.
Global grain reduces the uniform per-pixel glow that characterizes genuine organic-EL displays; the panel looks digitally noisy rather than phosphor-lit.
Track text and bottom-right status text are fine but the bottom strip overall feels slightly cluttered relative to the calm reference layout.
suggestions: Replace the halftone/dither interior of the dolphin with a solid, evenly-lit phosphor fill and reserve dithering only for a subtle shading gradient; keep a continuous bright rim-light edge so the form reads as one smooth object.
Re-draw the silhouette with crisp connected contours for rostrum, dorsal fin, pectoral fin and tail fluke so the leap looks graceful and anatomically legible at 320x128.
Eliminate or sharply attenuate the bottom-left bloom blob; render the VU segments as crisp, dim, discrete blocks consistent with the FFT bar styling.
Convert the under-dolphin fog into a short, motion-aligned persistence trail (a few fading ghost frames behind the arc) rather than a static vertical smear.
Lower overall noise and add a gentle Gaussian-style halo around crisp edges to emulate true OEL bloom — crisp core, soft surround, no interior stipple.
Nudge the dolphin's vertical extent toward 55-60% of display height to lock in dominance, while keeping the water lines at or below 15% and the FFT at ~13% as already achieved.
